claims.source: cSMAC formation was also impaired, because the same conjugates displayed a drastic reduction in the accumulation of Lck and PKC-θ at the cSMAC (Figure 2B,C).
claims.evidence: Confocal microscopy data showing reduced PKC-θ clustering with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Talin is required for F-actin polarisation to the synapse.
claims.source: Previous data have demonstrated that talin is required for F-actin polarisation to the synapse (Wernimont et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Wernimont et al., 2011.

claims.claim: 76.5% of conjugates formed with Zap70-active CTL show actin clearance into a ring at the dSMAC.
claims.source: The majority of conjugates formed with Zap70-active CTL accumulate actin at the contact site, which clears into a ring of actin at the dSMAC of the synapse (76.5%, n = 65) (Figure 3B, black) consistent with other studies of CTL (Tsun et al., 2011; Zhao et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: Quantitative confocal microscopy data showing actin clearance percentages, presented in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: 26% of conjugates formed with Zap70-inactive CTL show actin clearance.
claims.source: In contrast, when CTL lack Zap70 catalytic activity, they lose this ability, and the proportion of conjugates displaying clearance drops to 26% (n = 83) (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: Quantitative confocal microscopy data showing reduced actin clearance with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: 91.5% of conjugates lacking a cSMAC fail to clear actin when Zap70 is catalytically inhibited.
claims.source: When actin clearance is examined in conjugates which do not display a cSMAC (75%, n = 83), the effect is even more pronounced, with 91.5% of conjugates failing to clear actin.
claims.evidence: Quantitative confocal microscopy data analyzing actin clearance in conjugates without cSMAC.

claims.claim: Actin accumulates at the synapse in the absence of Zap70 catalytic activity.
claims.source: Interestingly, accumulation of actin at the synapse was still observed in the absence of Zap70 activity (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: Confocal microscopy data showing actin accumulation despite Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Phosphorylated ERK co-localises with actin at the immune synapse.
claims.source: Previous studies have shown that phosphorylated ERK may play a role in actin reorganisation as ERK co-localises with actin at the immune synapse, is implicated in granule and MTOC polarisation, and is required for CTL degranulation (Robertson et al., 2005; Jenkins et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Robertson et al., 2005 and Jenkins et al., 2009.

claims.claim: ERK is implicated in granule and MTOC polarisation.
claims.source: Previous studies have shown that phosphorylated ERK may play a role in actin reorganisation as ERK co-localises with actin at the immune synapse, is implicated in granule and MTOC polarisation, and is required for CTL degranulation (Robertson et al., 2005; Jenkins et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Robertson et al., 2005 and Jenkins et al., 2009.

claims.claim: ERK is required for CTL degranulation.
claims.source: Previous studies have shown that phosphorylated ERK may play a role in actin reorganisation as ERK co-localises with actin at the immune synapse, is implicated in granule and MTOC polarisation, and is required for CTL degranulation (Robertson et al., 2005; Jenkins et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Robertson et al., 2005 and Jenkins et al., 2009.

claims.claim: Zap70 phosphorylation on tyrosine 319 does not depend on Zap70 catalytic activity.
claims.source: Inhibition of Zap70 catalytic activity does not impair its capacity to be phosphorylated on tyrosine 319, which is inducibly phosphorylated upon CD3 crosslinking, and remains similarly phosphorylated in the presence of a high concentration of 3-MB-PP1 (10 μM).
claims.evidence: Western blot analysis showing Zap70 Y319 phosphorylation with and without inhibitor treatment.

claims.claim: Zap70 is a substrate of the upstream Src kinase Lck.
claims.source: This result is consistent with Zap70 as a substrate of the upstream Src kinase Lck.
claims.evidence: Inference from the observation that Zap70 Y319 phosphorylation persists when Zap70 catalytic activity is inhibited, combined with established knowledge.

claims.claim: LAT phosphorylation depends on Zap70 catalytic activity.
claims.source: However, the phosphorylation of LAT, a substrate of Zap70, as well as PLCγ and ERK all depend on Zap70 catalytic activity.
claims.evidence: Western blot analysis showing loss of LAT phosphorylation with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: PLCγ phosphorylation depends on Zap70 catalytic activity.
claims.source: However, the phosphorylation of LAT, a substrate of Zap70, as well as PLCγ and ERK all depend on Zap70 catalytic activity.
claims.evidence: Western blot analysis showing loss of PLCγ phosphorylation with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: ERK phosphorylation depends on Zap70 catalytic activity.
claims.source: However, the phosphorylation of LAT, a substrate of Zap70, as well as PLCγ and ERK all depend on Zap70 catalytic activity.
claims.evidence: Western blot analysis showing loss of ERK phosphorylation with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: A signalling pathway from Zap70 via the LAT signalosome and PLCγ is required for activation of ERK in CTL.
claims.source: These results suggest a signalling pathway from Zap70 via the LAT signalosome and PLCγ is required for activation of ERK in CTL.
claims.evidence: Inference from western blot data showing Zap70-dependent phosphorylation of LAT, PLCγ, and ERK.

claims.claim: A PI3K-dependent pathway is required for activating ERK and CTL degranulation.
claims.source: It has also been reported that a PI3K-dependent pathway is required for activating ERK and CTL degranulation (Robertson et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Robertson et al., 2005.

claims.claim: Akt phosphorylation is sensitive to Zap70 inhibition.
claims.source: Indeed, Akt phosphorylation was sensitive to Zap70 inhibition, suggesting that ERK is activated downstream of Zap70 through a LAT and PLCγ pathway or alternatively through a pathway that also includes AKT.
claims.evidence: Western blot analysis showing loss of Akt phosphorylation with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: ERK is activated downstream of Zap70 through a LAT and PLCγ pathway or alternatively through a pathway that also includes AKT.
claims.source: Indeed, Akt phosphorylation was sensitive to Zap70 inhibition, suggesting that ERK is activated downstream of Zap70 through a LAT and PLCγ pathway or alternatively through a pathway that also includes AKT.
claims.evidence: Inference from western blot data showing Zap70-dependent phosphorylation of LAT, PLCγ, ERK, and Akt.

claims.claim: Integrin activation occurs in the absence of Zap70 catalytic activity in naïve CD4 T cells.
claims.source: Since our previous studies had shown that integrin activation occurs in the absence of Zap70 catalytic activity in naïve CD4 T cells (Au-Yeung et al., 2010), we asked whether the integrin-mediated activation of Vav-1 (Gao et al., 2005) was seen in CTL in which Zap70 catalytic activity was inhibited.
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Au-Yeung et al., 2010.

claims.claim: Vav-1 plays an important role in both TCR- and integrin-mediated activation of actin reorganisation in T cells.
claims.source: This was of particular interest because Vav-1 has been shown to play an important role in both TCR- and integrin-mediated activation of actin reorganisation in T cells (del Pozo et al., 2003, Garcia-Bernal et al., 2009; Tybulewicz, 2005).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to del Pozo et al., 2003, Garcia-Bernal et al., 2009, and Tybulewicz, 2005.

claims.claim: TCR activation triggers Vav-1 phosphorylation independently of Zap70 kinase activity.
claims.source: We found that TCR activation triggers Vav-1 phosphorylation independently of Zap70 kinase activity, with Vav-1 phosphorylation occurring in both Zap70+/− and Zap70(AS) CTL lysates from cells treated with 3-MB-PP1, both for overall Vav-1 phosphorylation as well as at Y160, a site that is selectively phosphorylated upon TCR stimulation or αvβ3 integrin-mediated activation (Gao et al., 2005; Miletic et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: Western blot analysis of Vav-1 phosphorylation with and without Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 4B, combined with citations to Gao et al., 2005 and Miletic et al., 2006.

claims.claim: Vav-1 Y160 is selectively phosphorylated upon TCR stimulation or αvβ3 integrin-mediated activation.
claims.source: We found that TCR activation triggers Vav-1 phosphorylation independently of Zap70 kinase activity, with Vav-1 phosphorylation occurring in both Zap70+/− and Zap70(AS) CTL lysates from cells treated with 3-MB-PP1, both for overall Vav-1 phosphorylation as well as at Y160, a site that is selectively phosphorylated upon TCR stimulation or αvβ3 integrin-mediated activation (Gao et al., 2005; Miletic et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Gao et al., 2005 and Miletic et al., 2006.

claims.claim: Zap70 catalytic function makes only a minimal contribution to Vav-1 phosphorylation.
claims.source: Only a slight decrease in Vav1 phosphorylation is evident in Zap70(AS) CTL with 10 μM 3MB-PP1 suggesting Zap70 catalytic function makes only a minimal contribution to Vav-1 phosphorylation (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: Western blot analysis showing minimal reduction in Vav-1 phosphorylation with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: Vav-1 phosphorylation and GEF activation occur independently of Zap70 catalytic activity.
claims.source: These results suggest that Vav-1 phosphorylation, and presumably its GEF activation, occurs independently of Zap70 catalytic activity, while the pathway leading to ERK and PI3K activation are dependent on Zap70 catalytic activity.
claims.evidence: Inference from western blot data showing Vav-1 phosphorylation persists with Zap70 inhibition.

claims.claim: The pathway leading to ERK activation is dependent on Zap70 catalytic activity.
claims.source: These results suggest that Vav-1 phosphorylation, and presumably its GEF activation, occurs independently of Zap70 catalytic activity, while the pathway leading to ERK and PI3K activation are dependent on Zap70 catalytic activity.
claims.evidence: Western blot data showing loss of ERK phosphorylation with Zap70 inhibition.

claims.claim: The pathway leading to PI3K activation is dependent on Zap70 catalytic activity.
claims.source: These results suggest that Vav-1 phosphorylation, and presumably its GEF activation, occurs independently of Zap70 catalytic activity, while the pathway leading to ERK and PI3K activation are dependent on Zap70 catalytic activity.
claims.evidence: Western blot data showing loss of Akt phosphorylation (downstream of PI3K) with Zap70 inhibition.

claims.claim: Integrin activation occurs in CTL in which Zap70 is catalytically inhibited.
claims.source: This supports the idea that integrin activation occurs in CTL in which Zap70 is catalytically inhibited, as previously observed in Treg (Au-Yeung et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Inference from Vav-1 phosphorylation data combined with citation to Au-Yeung et al., 2010.

claims.claim: TCR activation increases the percentage of Zap70+/− CTL binding to ICAM-1 from 20% to 30%.
claims.source: TCR activation increased the percentage of CTL binding to ICAM-1 from 20% to 30% for Zap70+/− and from 16% to 34% for Zap70 (AS) CTL.
claims.evidence: Adhesion assay data showing increased binding to ICAM-1 after TCR activation, presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: TCR activation increases the percentage of Zap70(AS) CTL binding to ICAM-1 from 16% to 34%.
claims.source: TCR activation increased the percentage of CTL binding to ICAM-1 from 20% to 30% for Zap70+/− and from 16% to 34% for Zap70 (AS) CTL.
claims.evidence: Adhesion assay data showing increased binding to ICAM-1 after TCR activation, presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: 3-MB-PP1 treatment results in 32% binding to ICAM-1 for Zap70+/− CTL.
claims.source: 3-MB-PP1 treatment resulted in 32% binding for Zap70+/− and 25% for Zap70 (AS) CTL (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Adhesion assay data showing binding to ICAM-1 with inhibitor treatment, presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: 3-MB-PP1 treatment results in 25% binding to ICAM-1 for Zap70(AS) CTL.
claims.source: 3-MB-PP1 treatment resulted in 32% binding for Zap70+/− and 25% for Zap70 (AS) CTL (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Adhesion assay data showing binding to ICAM-1 with inhibitor treatment, presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: There is residual Zap70 catalytic-independent integrin function.
claims.source: While there does appear to be some reduction in CTL adhesion upon 3-MB-PP1 treatment, these data also suggest there is residual Zap70 catalytic-independent integrin function.
claims.evidence: Inference from adhesion assay data showing partial but not complete loss of adhesion with Zap70 inhibition.

claims.claim: CTL move with an average speed of 9 μm/min on an ICAM-1 surface when Zap70 is catalytically active.
claims.source: We found no difference in the speed of movement on an ICAM-1 surface with CTL moving with an average speed of 9 μm/min when Zap70 was catalytically active or inactive (Videos 1 and 2; n>84 each).
claims.evidence: Live cell imaging data measuring CTL movement speed, presented in Videos 1 and 2.

claims.claim: CTL move with an average speed of 9 μm/min on an ICAM-1 surface when Zap70 is catalytically inactive.
claims.source: We found no difference in the speed of movement on an ICAM-1 surface with CTL moving with an average speed of 9 μm/min when Zap70 was catalytically active or inactive (Videos 1 and 2; n>84 each).
claims.evidence: Live cell imaging data measuring CTL movement speed, presented in Videos 1 and 2.

claims.claim: Zap70 catalytic activity is not required for integrin activation in CTL.
claims.source: These results support the idea that Zap70 catalytic activity is not required for integrin activation in CTL.
claims.evidence: Inference from movement speed data showing no difference with Zap70 inhibition.

claims.claim: Conjugate formation is not impaired in Zap70-inactive CTL.
claims.source: Our finding that conjugate formation is not impaired in Zap70-inactive CTL also supports this model.
claims.evidence: Inference from conjugate formation data showing similar percentages with and without Zap70 inhibition.

claims.claim: Catalytically inhibited Zap70 can still participate in signal transduction without active catalysis by interacting with other signalling proteins via its phosphorylated tyrosines.
claims.source: Importantly, catalytically inhibited Zap70 can still participate in signal transduction without active catalysis, by interacting with other signalling proteins via its phosphorylated tyrosines.
claims.evidence: Inference from western blot data showing Zap70 phosphorylation persists with inhibitor treatment and established knowledge of protein-protein interactions.

claims.claim: Zap70 forms a complex with the adapter protein Crk, which activates the GTPase Rap1, which subsequently regulates integrin-mediated adhesion.
claims.source: These results in activated CTL are consistent with previous studies in naïve CD4 T cells, which demonstrated a Zap70 kinase-independent scaffold function, where Zap70 forms a complex with the adapter protein Crk, which activates the GTPase Rap1, which subsequently regulates integrin-mediated adhesion (Au-Yeung et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Au-Yeung et al., 2010.

claims.claim: Centrosome polarisation to the synapse is an important step in CTL killing.
claims.source: Centrosome polarisation to the synapse is an important step in CTL killing, because centrosome docking at the plasma membrane is responsible for directing the cytolytic granules to the secretory cleft at the cSMAC.
claims.evidence: Established knowledge about CTL killing mechanisms.

claims.claim: Centrosome docking at the plasma membrane is responsible for directing the cytolytic granules to the secretory cleft at the cSMAC.
claims.source: Centrosome polarisation to the synapse is an important step in CTL killing, because centrosome docking at the plasma membrane is responsible for directing the cytolytic granules to the secretory cleft at the cSMAC.
claims.evidence: Established knowledge about CTL killing mechanisms.

claims.claim: NK cells can polarise both centrosome and granules to the synapse in response to integrin activation alone.
claims.source: Given that NK cells can polarise both centrosome and granules to the synapse in response to integrin activation alone (Bryceson et al., 2005), it was of interest to ask whether the centrosome could polarise in CTL in which Zap70 was catalytically inhibited but integrin activation could still occur.
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Bryceson et al., 2005.

claims.claim: Lck is essential for docking of the centrosome at the plasma membrane in CTL.
claims.source: Our previous studies have shown that Lck is essential for docking of the centrosome at the plasma membrane since when Lck expression is inducibly turned off in mature CTL, the centrosome polarises towards the immune synapse, but does not dock at the plasma membrane.
claims.evidence: Reference to previous studies by the authors.

claims.claim: When Lck expression is turned off in mature CTL, the centrosome polarises towards the immune synapse but does not dock at the plasma membrane.
claims.source: Our previous studies have shown that Lck is essential for docking of the centrosome at the plasma membrane since when Lck expression is inducibly turned off in mature CTL, the centrosome polarises towards the immune synapse, but does not dock at the plasma membrane.
claims.evidence: Reference to previous studies by the authors.

claims.claim: In the absence of centrosome docking at the plasma membrane, the granules cannot be delivered to the immunological synapse and CTL killing is abolished.
claims.source: In the absence of centrosome docking at the plasma membrane, the granules cannot be delivered to the immunological synapse and CTL killing is abolished (Tsun et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Tsun et al., 2011.

claims.claim: Zap70 is a substrate of Lck.
claims.source: Zap70 is a substrate of Lck and its phosphorylation by Lck activates Zap70's kinase activity.
claims.evidence: Established knowledge about TCR signaling pathway.

claims.claim: Phosphorylation of Zap70 by Lck activates Zap70's kinase activity.
claims.source: Zap70 is a substrate of Lck and its phosphorylation by Lck activates Zap70's kinase activity.
claims.evidence: Established knowledge about TCR signaling pathway.

claims.claim: 65% of conjugates with catalytically active Zap70 display centrosomes tightly polarised to the cSMAC.
claims.source: The majority of conjugates (65%) with catalytically active Zap70, displayed centrosomes tightly polarised to the cSMAC (Figure 5B) (n = 118), in accordance with previously published work (Jenkins et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: Quantitative confocal microscopy data showing centrosome polarization percentages, presented in Figure 5B, with citation to Jenkins et al., 2009.

claims.claim: 54% of conjugates with catalytically inhibited Zap70 show a centrosome location >5 μm from the synapse.
claims.source: In contrast, Zap70 inhibition disrupted centrosome polarisation, with 54% of 3-MB-PP1 treated conjugates showing a centrosome location >5 μm from the synapse (Figure 5B) (n = 85).
claims.evidence: Quantitative confocal microscopy data showing impaired centrosome polarization with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: 44% of control Zap70(AS)+DMSO conjugates show granules tightly clustered to the synapse.
claims.source: Although the majority (44%) of control (Zap70(AS)+DMSO) conjugates (n = 117) show granules tightly clustered to the synapse, conjugates treated with 3-MB-PP1 showed a loss of granule polarisation to the synapse (Figure 5D) (n = 92).
claims.evidence: Quantitative confocal microscopy data showing granule polarization percentages, presented in Figure 5D.

claims.claim: Conjugates treated with 3-MB-PP1 show a loss of granule polarisation to the synapse.
claims.source: Although the majority (44%) of control (Zap70(AS)+DMSO) conjugates (n = 117) show granules tightly clustered to the synapse, conjugates treated with 3-MB-PP1 showed a loss of granule polarisation to the synapse (Figure 5D) (n = 92).
claims.evidence: Quantitative confocal microscopy data showing loss of granule polarization with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 5D.

claims.claim: The loss of centrosome and granule polarisation in cells lacking Zap70 catalytic activity is consistent with the loss of cytotoxicity.
claims.source: The loss of centrosome and granule polarisation in cells lacking Zap70 catalytic activity is consistent with the loss of cytotoxicity.
claims.evidence: Inference connecting polarization defects to cytotoxicity defects.

claims.claim: In contrast to NK cells, integrin activation is not sufficient for centrosome and granule polarisation to the synapse in CTL.
claims.source: These results suggest that, in contrast to NK cells, integrin activation is not sufficient for centrosome and granule polarisation to the synapse.
claims.evidence: Inference from data showing loss of polarization despite integrin activation in Zap70-inhibited CTL.

claims.claim: Zap70-active OT-I CTL show the centrosome polarising to the contact site within 6 min of initial interaction with the target.
claims.source: Live cell imaging of Zap70-active OT-I CTL show the centrosome polarising right up to the contact site within 6 min of initial interaction with the target (Figure 6; Video 3; n = 34).
claims.evidence: Live cell imaging data showing centrosome polarization kinetics, presented in Figure 6 and Video 3.

claims.claim: The centrosome begins to polarise towards the synapse in Zap70(AS) OT-I CTL treated with 3-MB-PP1 but fails to reach the contact site.
claims.source: However although the centrosome begins to polarise towards the synapse in Zap70(AS) OT-I CTL treated with 3-MB-PP1, the centrosome fails to reach the contact site with the closest point of contact ∼3 μm at 6 min after initial contact (Figure 6; Video 4; n = 50).
claims.evidence: Live cell imaging data showing aborted centrosome polarization with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 6 and Video 4.

claims.claim: In Zap-deficient CTL, centrosome polarisation begins but aborts before the centrosome docks at the contact site.
claims.source: In each video examined from Zap-deficient CTL, centrosome polarisation began, but aborted before the centrosome docked at the contact site formed by the synapse.
claims.evidence: Live cell imaging data showing consistent pattern of aborted centrosome polarization.

claims.claim: Contact sites formed between CTL with active Zap70 and target cells at 25 and 40 minutes show typical secretory synapses with flat stretches of tight membrane interactions and a central secretory cleft.
claims.source: At 25 (Figure 7A) and 40 (Figure 7C) minutes, the contact sites formed between CTL with active Zap70 and target cells show typical secretory synapses (Stinchcombe et al., 2001b) with flat stretches of tight membrane interactions between the cells surrounding a central intercellular gap between the two cell membranes, termed the secretory cleft.
claims.evidence: Electron microscopy data showing synapse ultrastructure, presented in Figure 7A and 7C, with citation to Stinchcombe et al., 2001b.

claims.claim: The secretory cleft forms an extracellular space containing heterogeneous membranous and granular material.
claims.source: The cleft forms an extracellular space containing heterogeneous membranous and granular material.
claims.evidence: Electron microscopy observations of secretory cleft contents.

claims.claim: Centrioles, lytic granules and Golgi elements are polarised up to the CTL plasma membrane in the middle of the contact site, opposite the secretory cleft.
claims.source: Centrioles, lytic granules and Golgi elements are polarised up to the CTL plasma membrane in the middle of the contact site, opposite the secretory cleft.
claims.evidence: Electron microscopy observations of organelle positioning.

claims.claim: At 40 min of CTL-target interaction, the target cell endoplasmic reticulum is slightly swollen and vacuolated, characteristic of target cell death.
claims.source: At these stages of interaction, the target cell appears relatively intact although the endoplasmic reticulum at 40 min is slightly swollen and vacuolated, characteristic of target cell death (Figure 7C).
claims.evidence: Electron microscopy observations of target cell morphology, presented in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: By 60 min of CTL-target interaction, there is marked evidence of target cell death with extensive endoplasmic reticular vacuolation and swollen mitochondria.
claims.source: By 60 min, there is marked evidence of target cell death with extensive endoplasmic reticular vacuolation and swollen mitochondria, with the CTL appearing to retract from an etiolated, dying target (Figure 7E).
claims.evidence: Electron microscopy observations of target cell death, presented in Figure 7E.

claims.claim: In the absence of Zap70 kinase activity, there is no evidence of tight, flat membrane–membrane associations between CTL and target.
claims.source: In the absence of Zap70 kinase activity the ultrastructure of the synapse is very different (Figure 7B,D,F). There is no evidence of the tight, flat membrane–membrane associations between CTL and target.
claims.evidence: Electron microscopy observations of synapse ultrastructure with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 7B, D, F.

claims.claim: Secretory clefts are absent in synapses formed by CTL lacking Zap70 kinase activity.
claims.source: Secretory clefts are absent, and neither centrioles, Golgi cisternae nor lytic granules are polarised towards the target cells.
claims.evidence: Electron microscopy observations of synapse ultrastructure with Zap70 inhibition.

claims.claim: Centrioles, Golgi cisternae and lytic granules are not polarised towards target cells in CTL lacking Zap70 kinase activity.
claims.source: Secretory clefts are absent, and neither centrioles, Golgi cisternae nor lytic granules are polarised towards the target cells.
claims.evidence: Electron microscopy observations of organelle positioning with Zap70 inhibition.

claims.claim: The contact site between CTL lacking Zap70 activity and targets is highly interdigitated, formed of long projections from the CTL surface.
claims.source: Instead, the contact site is highly interdigitated, formed of long projections from the CTL surface (black arrowheads).
claims.evidence: Electron microscopy observations of synapse morphology with Zap70 inhibition.

claims.claim: The only points of contact between CTL lacking Zap70 activity and target are at the tips of projections.
claims.source: Notably points of contact between CTL and target are restricted to the tips of projections, providing limited sites for receptor interactions between the cells.
claims.evidence: Electron microscopy observations of contact points with Zap70 inhibition.

claims.claim: Conjugates formed between CTL lacking Zap70 activity and targets after 25, 40 and 60 min of interaction show similar phenotypes.
claims.source: Conjugates formed between CTL lacking Zap70 activity and targets after 25, 40 and 60 min of interaction show similar phenotypes.
claims.evidence: Electron microscopy observations across multiple time points.

claims.claim: There is no evidence of target cell death at 25, 40, or 60 min in conjugates formed by CTL lacking Zap70 activity.
claims.source: There is no evidence of target cell death at any of these time points in these samples.
claims.evidence: Electron microscopy observations of target cell morphology with Zap70 inhibition.

claims.claim: The secretory cleft is absent in >85% of conjugates formed by Zap70(AS) CTL + 3-MB-PP1 at any time point.
claims.source: Quantitation of the EM data reveal that with Zap70(AS) CTL + 3-MB-PP1 the secretory cleft is absent in >85% of conjugates analysed at any time point (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A)
claims.evidence: Quantitative electron microscopy data, presented in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: The centrosome is found at distances greater than 1 μm from the synapse in >70% of conjugates formed by Zap70(AS) CTL + 3-MB-PP1.
claims.source: the centrosome is not docked and instead is found at distances greater than 1 μm from the synapse in >70% of conjugates (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B)
claims.evidence: Quantitative electron microscopy data, presented in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Projections are present between CTL and target in conjugates formed by Zap70(AS) CTL + 3-MB-PP1.
claims.source: and projections are present between CTL and target (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: Quantitative electron microscopy data, presented in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: Zap70(AS) CTL without inhibitor show secretory clefts in >50% of conjugates observed at 25 and 40 min.
claims.source: In contrast, in the absence of inhibitor Zap70(AS) CTL showed secretory clefts in >50% of conjugates observed at 25 and 40 min, reduced to 27% only at 60 min, when many of the target cells were dead.
claims.evidence: Quantitative electron microscopy data.

claims.claim: Zap70(AS) CTL without inhibitor show secretory clefts in 27% of conjugates at 60 min.
claims.source: In contrast, in the absence of inhibitor Zap70(AS) CTL showed secretory clefts in >50% of conjugates observed at 25 and 40 min, reduced to 27% only at 60 min, when many of the target cells were dead.
claims.evidence: Quantitative electron microscopy data.

claims.claim: 69% of conjugates formed by Zap70(AS) CTL without inhibitor at 25 min have at least one centriole <500 nm from the plasma membrane.
claims.source: Tightly polarised centrosomes are seen most frequently at the 25 min time-point when 69% of conjugates have at least one centriole <500 nm from the plasma membrane and 85% of conjugates show no projections between CTL and target.
claims.evidence: Quantitative electron microscopy data.

claims.claim: 85% of conjugates formed by Zap70(AS) CTL without inhibitor at 25 min show no projections between CTL and target.
claims.source: Tightly polarised centrosomes are seen most frequently at the 25 min time-point when 69% of conjugates have at least one centriole <500 nm from the plasma membrane and 85% of conjugates show no projections between CTL and target.
claims.evidence: Quantitative electron microscopy data.

claims.claim: Up to 60% of CTL lacking Zap70 catalytic activity show the centrosome within 3 μm of the synapse in conjugates formed at 25 min.
claims.source: Interestingly up to 60% of CTL lacking Zap70 catalytic activity show the centrosome within 3 μm of the synapse in conjugates formed at 25 min (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B), consistent with the initial polarisation up to this point observed in live imaging (Figure 6), decreasing to 35% in conjugates formed at 60 min.
claims.evidence: Quantitative electron microscopy data, presented in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: 35% of CTL lacking Zap70 catalytic activity show the centrosome within 3 μm of the synapse in conjugates formed at 60 min.
claims.source: Interestingly up to 60% of CTL lacking Zap70 catalytic activity show the centrosome within 3 μm of the synapse in conjugates formed at 25 min (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B), consistent with the initial polarisation up to this point observed in live imaging (Figure 6), decreasing to 35% in conjugates formed at 60 min.
claims.evidence: Quantitative electron microscopy data, presented in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The ultrastructural morphology of the synapse formed by CTL lacking Zap70 activity resembles that seen in wild-type CTL at very early stages of synapse formation.
claims.source: The unusual ultrastructural morphology of the synapse formed by CTL lacking Zap70 activity most closely resembles that seen in wild-type CTL at very early stages of synapse formation, when the target cell is intact and before the centrosome has polarised to the synapse (Figure 7G).
claims.evidence: Comparison of electron microscopy images, presented in Figure 7G.

claims.claim: At early stages of synapse formation in wild-type CTL, there are many interdigitations between CTL and target.
claims.source: At this stage of synapse formation there are many interdigitations between CTL and target and neither the flattening of the membranes between the two cells, nor the secretory cleft are seen.
claims.evidence: Electron microscopy observations of early synapse formation.

claims.claim: At early stages of synapse formation in wild-type CTL, the contact points between CTL and target are only found at the tips of projections.
claims.source: Here too the contact points between CTL and target are only found at the tips of projections between CTL and target.
claims.evidence: Electron microscopy observations of early synapse formation.

claims.claim: Loss of Zap70 catalytic activity arrests the reorganisation of membranes at the synapse at an early stage prior to formation of the secretory cleft.

results.result: Zap70 catalytic activity is required for CTL-mediated killing of target cells and for production of IFN-γ, TNF-α, and IL-2 cytokines. Inhibition of Zap70 with 3-MB-PP1 completely abrogates killing and cytokine production.
results.evaluation: Claims C1 and C2 are supported by cytotoxicity assays (Figure 1A) and FACS analysis (Figure 1B) showing complete loss of killing and cytokine production with Zap70 inhibition. The data are clear and quantitative with appropriate controls.

results.result: Conjugate formation between CTL and target cells occurs at similar frequencies (60% vs 67%) regardless of Zap70 catalytic activity, indicating that Zap70 catalytic activity is not required for initial CTL-target cell binding.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C4, and C43 are supported by quantitative microscopy data showing similar conjugate formation percentages with and without Zap70 inhibition. The small difference (7%) is not statistically significant and supports the conclusion that initial binding is Zap70-independent.

results.result: Zap70 catalytic activity is required for proper organization of the immunological synapse, including talin clearance into the pSMAC ring and accumulation of Lck and PKC-θ at the cSMAC. Without Zap70 activity, talin accumulates across the synapse and cSMAC formation is impaired.
results.evaluation: Claims C5-C8 are supported by confocal microscopy data (Figure 2A-C) showing impaired talin ring formation and reduced Lck/PKC-θ clustering with Zap70 inhibition. The imaging data are clear and quantified, demonstrating a drastic reduction in proper synapse organization.

results.result: Zap70 catalytic activity is required for actin clearance at the synapse. While 76.5% of Zap70-active CTL show actin clearance, only 26% of Zap70-inactive CTL clear actin, with 91.5% of conjugates lacking a cSMAC failing to clear actin. However, actin still accumulates at the synapse in the absence of Zap70 activity.
results.evaluation: Claims C10-C13 are supported by quantitative confocal microscopy data (Figure 3B-C) showing significant reduction in actin clearance with Zap70 inhibition while actin accumulation persists. The data clearly distinguish between actin accumulation and reorganization, with appropriate sample sizes (n=65-83).

results.result: Zap70 phosphorylation on Y319 persists when catalytic activity is inhibited, consistent with Zap70 as a substrate of Lck. However, phosphorylation of downstream targets LAT, PLCγ, ERK, and Akt all depend on Zap70 catalytic activity, suggesting a signaling pathway from Zap70 via LAT signalosome and PLCγ to ERK activation.
results.evaluation: Claims C17-C25 are supported by western blot data (Figure 4A) showing differential effects of Zap70 inhibition on upstream vs downstream phosphorylation events. The data clearly demonstrate that Zap70 can be phosphorylated when catalytically inactive but cannot phosphorylate its substrates, supporting the proposed signaling pathway.

results.result: Vav-1 phosphorylation, including at Y160, occurs independently of Zap70 catalytic activity, with only minimal reduction observed with Zap70 inhibition. This phosphorylation is likely mediated by Lck rather than Zap70.
results.evaluation: Claims C28-C31, C107, and C109 are supported by western blot data (Figure 4B) showing Vav-1 phosphorylation persists with Zap70 inhibition. The data are consistent across multiple phosphorylation sites and support the conclusion that Vav-1 activation is Zap70 catalytic activity-independent.

results.result: Integrin activation occurs in CTL lacking Zap70 catalytic activity, as evidenced by TCR-induced increases in ICAM-1 binding and normal CTL movement speed (9 μm/min) on ICAM-1 surfaces regardless of Zap70 activity. While some reduction in adhesion occurs with inhibitor treatment, residual Zap70 catalytic-independent integrin function remains.
results.evaluation: Claims C34-C42 are supported by adhesion assays (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and live cell imaging data (Videos 1-2) showing maintained integrin function with Zap70 inhibition. The movement speed data (n>84 each condition) are particularly compelling, showing no difference between active and inactive Zap70.

results.result: Zap70 catalytic activity is required for centrosome and granule polarization to the synapse. While 65% of conjugates with active Zap70 show centrosome polarization, 54% of inhibited conjugates show centrosomes >5 μm from the synapse. Similarly, granule polarization is lost with Zap70 inhibition. Unlike NK cells, integrin activation alone is insufficient for polarization in CTL.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C59 are supported by quantitative confocal microscopy data (Figure 5B, D) showing significant impairment of both centrosome and granule polarization with Zap70 inhibition. The data clearly distinguish CTL from NK cells and link polarization defects to loss of cytotoxicity.

results.result: Live cell imaging reveals that centrosome polarization in Zap70-active CTL reaches the contact site within 6 minutes. However, in Zap70-inhibited CTL, centrosome polarization initiates but aborts before docking, with the centrosome remaining ~3 μm from the contact site.
results.evaluation: Claims C60-C62 are supported by live cell imaging data (Figure 6, Videos 3-4) showing consistent patterns of aborted centrosome polarization in Zap70-inhibited CTL (n=50) compared to complete polarization in controls (n=34). The temporal resolution reveals the dynamic nature of this defect.

results.result: Electron microscopy reveals that synapses formed by Zap70-active CTL show typical secretory synapse ultrastructure with flat membrane contacts, secretory clefts, and polarized organelles, with progressive target cell death by 60 minutes. In contrast, Zap70-inhibited CTL form highly interdigitated contacts with long projections, no secretory clefts, no organelle polarization, and no target cell death at any time point.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C74 are supported by detailed electron microscopy observations (Figure 7A-F) across multiple time points (25, 40, 60 min). The ultrastructural differences are dramatic and consistent, providing clear evidence that Zap70 catalytic activity is required for proper membrane organization at the synapse.

results.result: Quantitative EM analysis shows that secretory clefts are absent in >85% of Zap70-inhibited conjugates, centrosomes are >1 μm from the synapse in >70% of conjugates, and projections are present. In contrast, Zap70-active CTL show secretory clefts in >50% of conjugates at 25-40 min, with 69% showing centrosomes <500 nm from the membrane at 25 min.
results.evaluation: Claims C75-C83 are supported by quantitative EM data (Figure 7—figure supplement 1) with adequate sample sizes (n=22-60 per condition). The quantitation confirms the qualitative observations and reveals temporal dynamics, including partial centrosome polarization (within 3 μm) in 60% of inhibited CTL at 25 min.

results.result: The ultrastructure of synapses formed by Zap70-inhibited CTL resembles early-stage wild-type synapses, with extensive interdigitations and contact points restricted to projection tips. This reveals that Zap70 catalytic activity arrests synapse formation at an early stage and establishes the first link between actin clearance and membrane flattening during synapse maturation.
results.evaluation: Claims C84-C89 are supported by comparative EM analysis (Figure 7G) showing similarity between Zap70-inhibited synapses and early wild-type synapses. The inference connecting actin-rich interdigitations to membrane organization is well-supported by the combined EM and confocal data.

results.result: In the absence of Zap70 catalytic activity, immunological synapse formation is arrested at a stage where actin-rich interdigitations dominate, actin accumulates across the synapse, TCR cannot coalesce to form a cSMAC, membranes cannot flatten, the secretory cleft does not form, downstream signaling is disrupted, and neither centrosome nor granules polarize.
results.evaluation: Claims C90-C96 represent a comprehensive summary of the major findings, supported by the full dataset including confocal microscopy, EM, western blots, and functional assays. Each component is well-documented by the preceding results.

results.result: Integrin-mediated actin dynamics proceed normally in Zap70-inactive CTL, with Vav-1 phosphorylation, actin accumulation at the synapse, and unimpaired integrin-mediated motility. However, Zap70 catalytic activity is required for actin reorganization (clearance) once the synapse has formed.
results.evaluation: Claims C110-C113 are supported by multiple lines of evidence including Vav-1 phosphorylation data, actin accumulation imaging, and movement speed measurements. The distinction between integrin-mediated accumulation and TCR-mediated reorganization is well-supported.

results.result: When Zap70 is catalytically active, actin clears centrally, membranes flatten, and TCR microclusters coalesce to form the cSMAC. Actin clearance is required for microcluster coalescence and marks a transition from highly interdigitated to flattened interfaces. Zap70 inhibition arrests synapse formation at an early stage.
results.evaluation: Claims C117-C120 synthesize the major findings and are supported by the combined confocal and EM data. The proposed model linking actin clearance to membrane flattening is well-supported by the ultrastructural observations, though the mechanism remains to be fully elucidated.

results.result: Unlike NK cells, CTL cannot polarize centrosome and granules in response to integrin activation alone. Zap70 has a novel role in controlling membrane reorganization to form the cSMAC and secretory cleft, and these rearrangements are essential for synapse function. Zap70 has distinct structural roles (regulating integrin-mediated actin control) versus catalytic roles (controlling TCR-mediated actin control and membrane remodeling).
results.evaluation: Claims C121-C124 represent the major conclusions of the study, supported by the comprehensive dataset. The distinction between structural and catalytic roles is well-supported by the Zap70(AS) system, which allows Zap70 to be phosphorylated and interact with partners while lacking catalytic activity.

results.result: The manuscript cites prior work establishing that: talin is required for F-actin polarization; ERK co-localizes with actin, is implicated in granule/MTOC polarization, and is required for CTL degranulation; PI3K is required for ERK activation and degranulation; integrin activation occurs without Zap70 catalytic activity in CD4 T cells; Vav-1 plays important roles in TCR- and integrin-mediated actin reorganization; NK cells can polarize in response to integrin activation alone; and Lck is essential for centrosome docking.
results.evaluation: Claims C9, C14-C16, C23, C26-C27, C29, C46-C53 are all supported by appropriate citations to prior literature. These provide the necessary context for interpreting the current findings.

results.result: The Zap70(AS) mouse model allows rapid and specific inhibition of Zap70 catalytic activity with 3-MB-PP1. Previous studies in CD4 cells showed that this inhibitor blocks LAT and ERK phosphorylation while Zap70 itself can still be phosphorylated and participate in signaling.
results.evaluation: Claims C97-C100 describe the experimental model and are supported by citations to prior work establishing the Zap70(AS) system. The current study confirms these properties in CTL.

results.result: The LAT signalosome and PLCγ are required for ERK activation in CTL, providing a rationale for previous observations implicating ERK and PLCγ in CTL-mediated killing.
results.evaluation: Claims C101-C103 are supported by the western blot data showing Zap70-dependent phosphorylation of LAT, PLCγ, and ERK, combined with appropriate citations. This connects the current findings to prior literature on CTL killing mechanisms.

results.result: Catalytically inactive Zap70 can be phosphorylated in CTL, supporting a kinase-independent scaffolding role in TCR regulation of integrin-mediated adhesion. The initial stages of synapse formation, with actin accumulation, may be integrin mediated.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C106 are supported by western blot data showing Zap70 phosphorylation with inhibitor treatment, combined with the observation that actin accumulation and integrin activation persist without Zap70 catalytic activity. The inference about integrin-mediated early synapse formation is reasonable but somewhat speculative.

results.result: Although earlier studies implicated Zap70 in Vav-1 activation, the current study shows Vav-1 phosphorylation occurs without Zap70 catalytic activity, likely mediated by Lck instead.
results.evaluation: Claims C108-C109 are supported by western blot data and appropriate citations. This represents a refinement of prior understanding, showing that Zap70's role in Vav-1 activation does not require its catalytic activity.

results.result: Zap70 is a substrate of Lck, and catalytically inhibited Zap70 can participate in signaling through its phosphorylated tyrosines. The pathways to ERK and PI3K activation depend on Zap70 catalytic activity. Zap70 forms complexes with Crk to activate Rap1 and regulate integrin-mediated adhesion.
results.evaluation: Claims C18, C32-C33, C44-C45 are supported by the western blot data and appropriate citations. These claims establish the mechanistic basis for distinguishing Zap70's structural versus catalytic roles.
